title: Perfecth
label: Matador Records
notes: Ninth album, nine songs; produced by Josh Homme and Michael Shuman. Earlier singles: 'Easy Street', 'Insignificant Other' (Aug. 25). Black vinyl, CD, deluxe limited LP. 2027 headline shows to be announced. Already in seed notes, re-verified.

title: Teen of Denial: Joe's Story (physical edition)
label: Matador Records
notes: Reworked 10th-anniversary version of Teens of Denial, with new mixes, changed lyrics, and new songs 'Optimistic Son' and 'Joe Drives Again'. It has been streaming since May 20, 2026; CD and 2xLP arrive Oct. 16. All profanity was removed, so it is radio-friendly.

title: The Ashram Tapes (Turiya Sings, Divine Songs, Infinite Chants, Glorious Chants)
label: Matador Records
notes: Announced July 2026 as the first complete authorized release of four devotional cassettes from the 1980s-90s. As of July the label said the date would be 'announced shortly'. No date found; it could slip to 2027. Spiritual jazz and devotional music, so it is outside the show's usual rock lane.

title: Autosmile
label: 4AD
pull_quote: This song was inspired by dead baby birds that kept appearing on my deck.
notes: Philadelphia art-folk duo (Victoria Rose and Stone Filipczak), pronounced 'at'. This is their first 4AD album (with Remote Control). Earlier singles: 'Autosmile' (nearly 7 minutes) and 'Punish My Mind'. They tour Oct. and Nov. 2026, plus a 2027 North American headline tour starting Jan. 16 in Philadelphia. The single date comes from the FEMMUSIC post dated Sept. 15.

title: The Gem
label: 4AD
latest_single: Get Away From Me (I Think I'll Love You Soon)
pull_quote: a bold and fun nod to eighties jangle rock and to the Melbourne sound she fell in love with
notes: Fourth album and her 4AD debut (with Remote Control). 10 tracks, produced by Robert Muinos and recorded above The Gem bar in Collingwood. She plays the Castro Theatre Oct. 23-24 (see seed notes). A 2026-27 tour is announced.

title: Horsepower
label: 4AD
notes: A 29-song triple album, debuted in full at the Ryman in Nashville on Aug. 22-23, 2026. Guests include Gillian Welch, Lucinda Williams and Iris DeMent. It is their twangiest, most Americana record. Lenker gave a soft target of spring or summer 2027. No official date yet, and the label is assumed to be 4AD (their last album, Double Infinity, was 4AD); no source confirmed it.
